Hi Dana —

Thanks again for carving out time for the performance run last week. We pulled together a concise debrief that walks through the latency distributions, end-to-end traces, and a couple of follow-up asks so your engineering/security/procurement teams have what they need to evaluate the next steps.

Would love to lock a 60-minute debrief with your engineers + security + procurement so we can:
- Walk through p50/p95/p99 from the runs and the workload profile
- Show KV-cache behavior and warm/cold token effects
- Agree on any additional artifacts you need for procurement/security review

Two windows we have available next week (PT):
- Tue 2027-02-16: 10:30–11:30 or 15:00–16:00
- Wed 2027-02-17: 13:00–14:00

If none of those work, send a few options and we’ll flex. Please loop in procurement/security contacts so we can cover their asks live. Attached a short quicknotes PDF summarizing the runs (high-level).

Attachments: redwood-benchmark-quicknotes.pdf (summary, 2 pages)

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0142

- Procurement wants an abbreviated cost estimate for a steady-state Dedicated profile (monthly) and an outline of support/SLA options to include in our internal packet.

Best windows for our engineers (PT) next week are: Tue 2027-02-16 after 16:00 or Thu 2027-02-18 between 09:00–11:30.

Looping in our security lead (security-contact@nestpay.com) and procurement. Attendees from our side will be: Dana Lee (platform), Omar Rios (SRE), and Priya Shah (procurement).

Hi Dana / team —

Thanks for the quick reply — happy to run the technical portion. Quick answers to the asks above and a suggested run of show: 

Pre-read / artifacts we can share ahead of the meeting (attached):
- redwood-benchmark-quicknotes.pdf (vanessa attached)
- kvcache-sample.tar.gz (small artifact showing cache hit/miss traces)
- perf-traces-sanitized.log (we'll upload to the Drive link Vanessa included)

What we need from you before the call (short checklist):
- A sample request/response pair (anonymized) or a clear description of tokenization pattern and avg prompt length
- Your expected steady-state QPS and peak burst QPS for the scenario you'd like to discuss
- Any network constraints (e.g., private VPC, egress controls) or HSM/KMS requirements for keying

Proposed run of show (60 min):
1) 5 min — introductions & goals (Vanessa / Dana)
2) 20 min — results walk (p50/p95/p99, throughput floors)
3) 15 min — traces and KV-cache behavior (warm vs cold)
4) 10 min — procurement/security Q&A
5) 10 min — next steps / action items (procurement follow-ups, test artifacts)

From the options you gave, we can do: Thu 2027-02-18 09:30–10:30 PT (this hits both SE and my schedule). If you prefer Tue after 16:00, we're available 16:30–17:30 PT on 2027-02-16 but that will be tight for our East Coast folks.

Attaching the KV cache sample (stub) for their security team to inspect — it contains only synthesized keys and timing traces, no customer data.

Attachments: kvcache-sample.tar.gz (artifact stub)

Let me know which slot you prefer and we’ll send a calendar invite and a Drive link for the sanitized traces.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
